reasoning: The document contains 1 major LLM fidelity defect related to hyperlinks being extracted as standalone elements rather than inline with the text. Programmatic signals strongly corroborate this finding, identifying 16 displaced links. Following the count-based routing rules, the presence of a major defect requires HUMAN_REVIEW.

concerns.description: Link text pulled over but not hyperlinked
concerns.analysis: On page 3, several clickable links in the source PDF text are pulled into the JSON as flat, plain text without being properly split into link elements inline. For example, 'security awareness training', 'Facebook', 'LinkedIn', 'it.nc.gov/CyberSecureNC', and 'Stay Safe Online' are embedded directly within their respective plain text paragraphs without being wrapped as clickable links.

concerns.output_quote: {"type": "paragraph", "text": "New-school security awareness training can give your organization an essential layer of defense against evolving social engineering attacks."}

concerns.description: Displaced hyperlinks: 16 link(s) extracted as standalone elements instead of inline text
concerns.analysis: standalone_links=16, examples=['https://www.knowbe4.com/resource-center/phishing', 'https://www.knowbe4.com/what-is-social-engineering', 'https://www.knowbe4.com/resource-center/phishing']. Links should be inline within paragraphs, not separate blocks.

On page 3 of the source PDF, several text segments are underlined to indicate they are hyperlinks (e.g., 'X', 'Facebook', 'LinkedIn', 'Read the SAC newsletters.', 'security awareness training'). In the extraction JSON, these words are included as plain text in the paragraph blocks without any underline formatting or markdown link representation.
